paper.title: The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students’ Creative Idea Generation: Switching Effects in Repeated Task Performance
paper.venue: The Journal of Korean Association of Computer Education
paper.pdf_filename: Kang et al (2026) - The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students' Creative Idea Generatio.pdf
paper.version_read: Published journal version: Kang and Kim (2026), The Journal of Korean Association of Computer Education, 29(6), 40-49, doi:10.32431/kace.2026.29.6.004. PDF p. 1 (printed p. 40) gives publication date 2026-06-22. Korean main text with English title and abstract.
paper.one_line_finding: Students randomly given AI for the round-2 upgrade raised their 0-100 rubric creativity score by 28.63 points more than students kept without AI (SE 2.49, 95% CI [23.74, 33.52]; gains 37.73 vs 9.10), and students randomly cut off from AI gained 5.50 points less than those who kept it (SE 2.47, p = .026) (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.4.2; Table 4).

arms.name: A1 (maintain AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in the initial draft and maintained for the upgrade; randomized within initial group A.

arms.name: A2 (discontinue AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in the initial draft and removed for the upgrade; randomized within initial group A. The generative_ai code records prior exposure; the scored upgrade was produced without AI.

arms.name: B1 (adopt AI)
arms.description: Initial draft produced without AI; generative AI introduced for the upgrade, randomized within initial group B.

arms.name: B2 (maintain no AI)
arms.description: No AI in either the initial draft or the upgrade; randomized within initial group B.

studies.task: Students generated up to 10 ideas for improving life in 2035 during a 10-minute initial round, then revised, supplemented, or elaborated their own ideas for 10 minutes after an approximately 30-minute break in the same session (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (Free plan; version available by default at the time), with other generative AI tools also permitted
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1, continuation of step (1); no underlying model version or release year specified

preregistration.where: No preregistration or registry is mentioned in the document.

estimates.outcome: Gain in total creativity score from initial draft to upgrade (H3)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent raters, blind to condition, scored each idea on novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, and future-change fit. Idea scores range from 0 to 10; scores for up to 10 ideas are summed to a participant total ranging from 0 to 100, and the two raters' totals are averaged. Similar or duplicate ideas within a participant's round receive novelty deductions. The analyzed outcome here is the participant's round-2 total minus round-1 total. The total combines idea quantity and quality. Rater expertise is not stated; measure is null because neither lay-rater nor expert-rater status is confirmed. Scoring: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4.

stats.difference_is: Treatment minus control in mean gain (each gain is round-2 total minus round-1 total)

regression.model: Planned contrast of time-by-condition effects from the linear mixed-effects model score ~ time * round_2_group + (1 | participant), with A1 as the reference condition. The model includes all analyzed participants; the contrast compares the two arms within one initial-group randomization stratum. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.4.

sources.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Section 4.4.2, H3 planned contrast

estimates.notes: AI adoption during the upgrade versus continued non-use. Both arms produced their initial draft without AI. All statistics refer to gains; the reported positive contrast is B1 gain minus B2 gain. This is a paper-designated main planned contrast (PDF p. 6, printed p. 45, Section 3.3.4), but no preregistration is reported. SDs describe participant-level change scores, not individual ideas or separate ratings. No days-long follow-up is reported; both rounds were in the same session. The model accounts for within-participant repeated measurements with a random intercept. Reconciliation confirmed the between-person randomized comparison within the entire initial-condition stratum. within_person is null: repeated outcome measurement does not make this a randomized-order crossover. n_total is the printed count of people in the two contrasted arms, rather than all people contributing to the mixed model. The positive gain contrast indicates more creative output on the summed rubric. The separately retained round-2 endpoint record uses the same participants and is not an independent effect. For selection among gain and endpoint specifications, this paper-designated main gain contrast takes precedence.
estimates.primary_override_reason: with_ai, ai_vs_bau. Both candidates are randomized within an initial group (the initial A/B allocation is not described as random). B1 versus B2 compares AI access with no AI among people who had not used AI before, as in single-session studies; A1 versus A2 compares keeping with withdrawing AI after an AI-assisted first draft.

estimates.notes: Added at reconciliation: Table 4 reports participant-level endpoint means, SDs, and counts for the same full randomized arm pair as the corresponding gain contrast. These are descriptive endpoint data; the paper tests the gain contrast and prints no endpoint difference, SE, CI, test, p-value, or standardized effect. All such endpoint fields remain null. se_basis is not_reported because no uncertainty for an endpoint contrast is printed; the arm SDs are participant-level dispersion. This is a between-person comparison within an initial-condition stratum, so within_person is null. The treatment arm had AI available during the scored upgrade, supporting with_ai and outcome_with_ai true. Both rounds occurred in the same session. No days-based delay is calculated. The endpoint and gain records reuse the same participants and are not independent. The paper-designated main gain specification takes precedence for primary-record selection. form_outcome_id is null because the screening form represents this randomized pair through the gain outcome S1-O1 and does not assign an ID to its endpoint specification.

not_extracted.what: S2-O1: round-one total creativity, A (AI) versus B (no AI), H1
not_extracted.reason: Assignment to the initial A/B groups is not described as random. All explicit randomization statements concern the subsequent within-group split. Therefore this comparison does not meet the randomized-assistance requirement, despite printed means, SDs, Welch test, CI, and Cohen d. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 4.2; allocation, PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 43-44), Section 3.1. Screening study S2 is not an additional independent sample.

not_extracted.what: S2-O2: unassisted round-two total creativity, A2 (prior AI) versus B2 (never AI)
not_extracted.reason: This after_ai comparison crosses initial groups whose allocation is unstated; random splitting within A and B does not establish random prior-AI exposure between them. Only arm descriptives are printed, and no A2 versus B2 test is reported. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 4; allocation, PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1.

not_extracted.what: Round-one balance tests: A1 versus A2 and B1 versus B2
not_extracted.reason: Both arms in each pair had the same AI availability when the baseline outcome was produced. These are checks before the randomized switching intervention, not its effects. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.1 and Table 1.

not_extracted.what: Pooled round-one to round-two total-creativity change, H2
not_extracted.reason: The paired comparison pools all AI histories and measures repetition/upgrade over time; it has no randomized AI-versus-comparison contrast. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Section 4.3, Table 2 and Figure 2.

not_extracted.what: Within-arm paired changes for A1, A2, B1 and B2, and the A1 mixed-model time effect
not_extracted.reason: These compare successive task stages within a single arm. Task-stage order was fixed, not randomized, and these are not paired randomized-order AI contrasts. Table 3 paired tests and dz values, and the reference-arm time coefficient, must not be used as between-arm effects or uncertainty. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 3 and Section 4.4.2.

not_extracted.what: Switching asymmetry, (B1 minus B2 gain) minus (A1 minus A2 gain), H5
not_extracted.reason: This compares the two treatment effects across initial-AI strata and is an effect-modification contrast, not an additional two-arm AI assistance contrast. Initial A/B assignment is also unstated. Excluded under the rule against moderation results. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 47), Section 4.4.2, item 3.
Only whole-sample means by round are reported; no counts or contrasts by AI arm, SDs, or uncertainty are given. No randomized AI contrast can be transcribed. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.2.2.

not_extracted.what: Total-score interrater reliability (single-rater and average-rater ICCs)
not_extracted.reason: Agreement between raters is not a treatment contrast on creative output. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.2.4.

open_items: Initial assignment to A versus B is not described as random. The screening form's S2 comparisons remain ineligible unless that allocation can be confirmed.

The number assigned and the number excluded are not printed. Only students who completed both rounds were analyzed, so n_randomized remains null for the study and arms (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).

The background of the two independent human raters is not stated; measure is null because neither human_raters (lay raters or crowd workers) nor expert_raters is confirmed (PDF p. 6, printed p. 45, Section 3.2.4).
The exact ChatGPT model, its release year, and which alternative generative AI tools were actually used are not reported; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).
The paper does not report arm-level idea counts, mean quality per idea, or separate rubric-dimension effects, so quantity and quality cannot be separated from the total.
No preregistration, supplementary appendix, or posted-data location is stated in the document.
